definition_concordance.source_concept: A_d: real Schwartz functions with fhat(0)>0, fhat>=0, and f<=0 outside the unit ball
definition_concordance.analysis: The Lean carrier is complex-valued Schwartz with explicit real-valuedness of f and fhat; source nonnegativity of fhat already entails a real Fourier value. The sign radius is exactly 1 and fhat(0)>0 is explicit.
The numerator and denominator are the real parts of values already constrained to be real; the denominator is strictly positive.

definition_concordance.source_concept: LP_d = v_d/2^d * inf_{f in A_d} f(0)/fhat(0)
definition_concordance.analysis: The same unit-ball volume, factor 2^d, quotient and infimum normalization are used.

definition_concordance.source_concept: radial reduction does not change the quotient infimum
definition_concordance.analysis: Every radial admissible function embeds into the full class, and every full admissible function is radialized with quotient preserved. Consequently the full and radial quotient sets and linear programs are equal, so no radiality restriction silently strengthens the source statement.

field_audit.analysis: This is the quotient-root asymptotic sInf(root quotient)/sqrt(d) -> 1/pi. It is a reformulation of the LP asymptotic under the exact v_d/2^d normalization, not the Fourier sign-uncertainty Theorem 1.2 despite sharing the constant 1/pi.
The error is defined from the normalized quotient-root sequence and tends to zero. For d>0 the displayed equality is algebraic. This adds an explicit witness function but no asymptotic strength.
The limit fullLinearProgram(d)^(1/d) -> sqrt(e/(2*pi)) is the source headline theorem under the proved full/radial equality.
Taking logarithms of the eventually positive LP sequence gives log(LP_d)/d -> (1/2) log(e/(2*pi)). The formal proof establishes the positivity needed for the logarithm step.
The field rewrites the root limit as an eventually exact d-th-power formula with an additive root error tending to zero. The error is explicitly constructed from LP_d^(1/d)-sqrt(e/(2*pi)).

field_audit.lean_dependency: exists_manuscriptUniversalPackingIsLittleO <- manuscriptPackingDeficit_nonneg + manuscriptUniversalQuotientBound; transported from radial to full admissibles by quotient-preserving radialization
field_audit.analysis: The source gives epsilon_d -> 0 uniformly for every admissible F. Lean chooses delta_d = max(0, criticalPackingBase-LP_d^(1/d)), so delta_d is nonnegative and tends to zero; replacing an arbitrary signed source error by this deficit only weakens the lower base when needed and the universal quotient bound is proved. No claim that the source itself states epsilon_d>=0 is made.

field_audit.source_locus: displayed alpha_* formula immediately after Theorem 1.1
field_audit.analysis: The source identifies alpha_*=(1/2)log_2(2*pi/e)=0.6044..., hence positivity is a consequence, not a separately advertised theorem. Lean proves positivity from exact inequalities rather than from the decimal expansion.

field_audit.source_locus: exact alpha_* formula after Theorem 1.1; source prints only 0.6044...
field_audit.analysis: Lean proves alpha_* lies strictly between 0.604400544291677695341677307053 and 0.604400544291677695341677307054. This 30-decimal enclosure is not printed in the manuscript and must never be represented as source-authored numerical precision; it is admitted only as a checked mathematical consequence of the manuscript's exact alpha_* expression.
The normalized base-two logarithm tends to -alpha_*, exactly matching the displayed exponential-rate consequence of Theorem 1.1.

The formal error is -(log_2 LP_d)/d-alpha_* and tends to zero; eventual positivity of LP_d allows exact reconstruction LP_d=2^(-(alpha_*+err_d)d). This is an explicit witness form of the manuscript's o(1), not a stronger rate estimate.
